1.title: Subscriptions, Management Groups, Policy, Locks, Tags and Costs
1.text: Welcome to Module three: Subscriptions, Management Groups, Policy, Locks, Tags and Costs. It covers the exam area Manage Azure identities and governance. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Implement and manage Azure Policy. Configure resource locks. Apply and manage tags. Manage resource groups. Manage subscriptions. Manage costs by using alerts, budgets and Azure Advisor recommendations. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Manage Azure identities and governance (twenty-twenty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: The organization structure
1.text: The organization structure. The figure shows this: Management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and resources.

1.title: The organization structure, continued
1.text: The organization structure. Management group. Container for subscriptions; apply policy and R B A C once for many subscriptions; nest up to six levels below the root. Subscription. Billing and access boundary; also holds quotas. Resource group. Logical container for resources with the same lifecycle. Resource. The Azure service instance. A resource group has a location only for its metadata; its resources can be in other regions. Deleting a resource group deletes everything in it. Resources can be moved between resource groups and subscriptions (not all types). Subscriptions can be moved between management groups. Exam tip: "Apply the same policy to many subscriptions" equals a management group.

1.title: Azure Policy
1.text: Azure Policy. Azure Policy makes sure resources follow your rules (allowed regions, required tags, allowed sizes). It evaluates resources and can block, flag or fix them. Policy definition. One rule with a condition and an effect. Initiative. A group of definitions managed together. Assignment. Applies a definition or initiative to a scope (with optional exclusions). Effects. Deny (block the request), Audit (flag only), Append or Modify (add or change properties such as tags), Deploy If Not Exists (deploy a related resource). Remediation task. Fixes existing non-compliant resources (needs a managed identity). Compliance. The dashboard of compliant and non-compliant resources. Exam tip: Policy checks the resource's properties (what is allowed). R B A C controls the user's permissions (who can act). "Prevent creating V Ms outside two regions" equals Policy with Deny.

1.title: Resource locks
1.text: Resource locks. Delete (Can Not Delete). Users can read and modify, but cannot delete. Read-only. Users can only read; no changes or deletes. Locks apply to a subscription, resource group or resource, are inherited by child resources, and override R B A C permissions, even for Owners. To change a locked resource you must remove the lock first.

1.title: Tags
1.text: Tags. Tags are name-value pairs on resources, resource groups and subscriptions (for example Environment Production, Cost Center one thousand two hundred thirty-four ). Use them to organize, report on cost and automate. Inheritance. Tags are not inherited from resource groups by default; use Azure Policy (Modify or Append) to apply or inherit them. Cost. Cost analysis can group by tag. Limit. Up to fifty tag pairs per resource.

1.title: Costs
1.text: Costs. Cost analysis. See and break down spending (by resource group, tag, service). Budgets. Set a spending threshold and alerts; a budget does not stop spending. Cost alerts. Notify at budget percentages or on anomalies. Azure Advisor. Recommendations for cost, reliability, security, operational excellence and performance (for example, resize or shut down underused V Ms). Exam tip: A budget alerts you; it does not shut resources down. To stop spending automatically you must act on the alert (for example an action group that runs automation).

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. An organization wants to prevent resources from being created outside two approved regions in all subscriptions. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: An Azure Policy assignment with a Deny effect at a management group. Policy with Deny at a management group enforces the region rule across subscriptions.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An administrator wants users to modify a production storage account but never delete it. What should be applied? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A Delete (Can Not Delete) lock. A Can Not Delete lock allows changes but blocks deletion.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An Owner cannot delete a resource. What is the likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A resource lock. Locks override even Owner permissions.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Resources should inherit the Cost Center tag from their resource group. What should the administrator use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: An Azure Policy with the Modify effect. Tags are not inherited by default; a Modify policy can apply them.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team wants an email when spending reaches eighty percent of the monthly plan. What should be created? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A budget with an alert. Budgets send alerts at configured thresholds.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which tool recommends resizing underused virtual machines to save money? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Azure Advisor. Advisor gives cost and other recommendations.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the purpose of a management group? Answer: To organize subscriptions and apply policy and R B A C across them. Question two. Name two Azure Policy effects. Answer: For example Deny and Audit (also Modify, Append, Deploy If Not Exists). Question three. What does a Read-only lock allow? Answer: Only reading; no changes or deletions.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Are tags inherited by default? Answer: No. Question five. Does a budget stop spending? Answer: No, it only alerts. Question six. What happens when a resource group is deleted? Answer: All its resources are deleted.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Hierarchy: management group greater than subscription greater than resource group greater than resource. Policy: definition, initiative, assignment; Deny, Audit, Modify, Deploy If Not Exists; remediation. Locks: Can Not Delete, Read-only; inherited; override R B A C. Tags: name-value pairs; not inherited; group costs by tag. Costs: budgets and alerts (no auto-stop), cost analysis, Advisor.
